IndieWire's 50 Best Horror Directors of All Time

articles.summary: Tobe Hooper's forgotten, maligned blend of horror and soft-core erotica arrives on Blu-ray in all its nude horseback riding, snake charming, eyeball-gouging glory, just in time for Halloween.
articles.content: Director Tobe Hooper is simultaneously one of horror’s most celebrated filmmakers and one of its most underrated — celebrated thanks to his direction of one of the most influential and accomplished horror movies of all time, “ The Texas Chainsaw Massacre ,” but underrated given the overall lack of appreciation for most of what came after. Credit for Hooper’s biggest hit, “Poltergeist,” is generally (and erroneously) attributed to producer Steven Spielberg . Elsewhere, though Hooper’s TV adaptation of “Salem’s Lot” has gained stature in recent years, he’s generally discussed as a director whose work lives in the shadow of “Chainsaw” — when he’s discussed at all. Some of these movies are not only forgotten but were barely known to begin with, given Hooper’s termite-like existence in the 1990s and 2000s, decades spent toiling in low-budget straight-to-DVD indies, and anonymous cable television assignments. Thankfully, boutique physical media labels like Arrow, Shout! articles.content: Barbara Barrie , who received a Tony nomination for her role in Broadway’s original Company , an Oscar nomination for her performance in Breaking Away and wide recognition as the wife of Hal Linden’s police captain on TV’s Barney Miller , died October 28 at her home in Manhattan. She was 95. Her death was reported to The New York Times by her daughter Jane Harnick, who said Barrie’s death was medically assisted and that the actor had been diagnosed with terminal cancer. Following her breakthrough Cannes Film Festival award-winning performance in 1964’s One Potato, Two Potato , Barrie built a career that encompassed the stage, film and television, making marked contributions to all. She appeared in 11 Broadway productions, including original stagings of Stephen Sondheim’s Company , Neil Simon’s The Prisoner of Second Avenue and California Suite , Harvey Fierstein’s Torch Song Trilogy and a 2004 revival of Fiddler on the Roof . In addition to 1979’s Breaking Away , her film credits included an uncredited role in the classic 1956 drama Giant and as the mother of Goldie Hawn’s character in 1980’s Private Benjamin. Barrie was most prolific on television, with credits stretching back to the 1950s anthology dramas and such popular 1960s series as Route 66, The Twilight Zone, The Fugitive, Ben Casey and Ironside, among many others. In 1974 she flirted with Gavin MacLeod’s Murray Slaughter on a memorable episode of The Mary Tyler Moore Show and began her five-season recurring role on Barney Miller the following year. Her character largely was absent beyond the first season as the ABC sitcom increasingly focused on the police precinct workplace comedy rather than the title character’s domestic life. In addition to her portrayal of Barney Miller ‘s Liz Miller, Barrie probably is best known to TV audiences for her series regular role on the 1996-2000 sitcom Suddenly Susan , in which she portrayed “Nana” Keane, grandmother of Brooke Shields’ title character. articles.title: Milwaukee Brewers Win First World Series In Franchise History
articles.content: The now-departed Uecker, more famous for his beer commercials than he ever was for his modest career as a MLB catcher, was the Milwaukee Brewers’ radio announcer until 2024. And tonight, as the team won its first-ever World Series , his 54 years in the booth were not forgotten. In his postgame locker room speech tonight, Brewers’ manager Pat Murphy carried on his schtick of delivering Uecker’s “messages” to the team from the great beyond. “So, Ueck sent me a text today. He said, ‘Look, I helped you against the Padres. And I messed with the Dodgers a little bit. And then you came here, and you were on your own, because we had a doubleheader and they actually let me catch the last three innings of the game. But you did it for the city, you did it for the state, and you boys oughta be awfully proud to know that you’re the first-ever Milwaukee Brewer team to be world champions.'” Not that the Brewers needed any help. They were clearly the best team in Major League Baseball all season. They had the best record and stormed through the postseason, sweeping the two-time defending champion L.A. Dodgers to win the NLCS and beating the Tampa Bay Rays in a gentleman’s sweep, four games to one, in the World Series. In that’s quite a feat for the team from the league’s smallest market especially since, in its 57 years of existence, the club had never won the final game of the season. After taking each of the first two games in this year’s World Series by one run, the Brewers destroyed the Rays 10-0 in Game 3. Tampa Bay regained some dignity last night with a 4-3 win before being dominated again tonight. Milwaukee led from the second inning on. They went up 4-0 in the 6th when Brewers catcher William Contreras (later named series MVP) drove in Christian Yelich to score the team’s final run. Tampa Bay got some consolation in the bottom of the 9th when Chandler Simpson doubled to deep right field and brought Liam Hicks in to score. But it was Milwaukee’s night — and year.

articles.title: now-departed
articles.content: Bob Uecker , a a Baseball Hall of Famer who spent 54 years as the Milwaukee Brewers play-by-play man, starred in the 1980s sitcom Mr. Belvedere and had a memorable roles in the movie Major League and in Miller Lite ads, died Thursday. He was 90. The Brewers announced the news, saying in part: “Ueck was the light of the Brewers, the soundtrack of our summers, the laughter in our hearts, and his passing is a profound loss. He was the heart and soul of Wisconsin and a dear friend. …. He was a national treasure.” Read the team’s full statement below. Known for his often self-deprecating wit and warm smile, Uecker had an uneventful six-year MLB career with the Brewers and three other teams in the 1960s. He worked briefly as a scout before joining the Atlanta Braves broadcast team for two seasons. He began his legendary run as the Brewers announcer in 1971 and also called national network games. He was the fourth-longest-tenured announced in Major League Baseball history and was inducted into the inaugural class of the Brewers’ Wall of Honor in 2014. Uecker likely is best known among non-sports fans for playing frumpy sportswriter George Owens on ABC’s Mr. Belvedere from 1985-90. He and wife Marsha (Ilene Graff) hire debonair English housekeeper Lynn Belvedere (Christopher Hewett), who is proficient as cooking, cleaning and solving the family’s problems. Airing mostly on Friday nights, the comedy never made the primetime year-end Top 30 in the three-network universe but lasted six seasons. During that show’s run, he also played Harry Doyle, the put-upon homer announcer in the 1989 movie Major League, starring Charlie Sheen, Tom Berenger and others. After the Big League pitch by Sheen’s hot prospect Rick “Wild Thing” Vaughn goes all the way to the backstop, Doyle says, “Juuuuust a bit outside — he tried the corner with it.” He reprised the role in 1994’s Major League II and 1998’s Major League: Back to the Minors. articles.content: This pummelling Netflix production seeks pathos amid the gunfire as it tells the true story of four college football stars joining the Marines in the wake of Pearl Harbor, but not one of these noble warriors feels like a real person. Ostensibly, Berg’s Netflix -backed combat epic is fighting the same fight as Terrence Malick’s “The Thin Red Line,” likewise charting the physical and psychological torment of American soldiers in Guadalcanal during the Pacific Theater of the Second World War. articles.title: Barbara Barrie, Oscar-Nominated Star of ‘Barney Miller’ and ‘Breaking Away,’ Dies at 95
articles.content: Barbara Barrie , the Oscar-, Emmy- and Tony-nominated actress who starred in the original production of “Company” and in films including “Breaking Away,” died Wednesday in Manhattan. She was 95. Her daughter confirmed her death to the New York Times and said Barrie’s death was medically assisted following a terminal cancer diagnosis. On stage, Barrie made her Broadway debut in 1955 in “The Wooden Dish,” and went on to perform in roles across Broadway and off for more than 60 years until she took her last bow in “Significant Other.” She starred in 1976’s “California Suite,” 1958’s “The Crucible,” and in both “A Midsummer Night’s Dream” and “The Taming of the Shrew” from 1958-1959. She was, most notably, a member of the original Broadway cast of “Company,” Stephen Sondheim’s acclaimed 1970s musical. She was nominated for a Tony for best featured actress in a musical for the role of Sarah. In 1979, she starred in “Breaking Away,” which was nominated for five Oscars. She earned a best supporting actress nod for her role. On television, Barrie appeared on shows including “The Defenders,” “Naked City,” “Twilight Zone,” “The Alfred Hitchcock Hour,” “Barney Miller” and “Suddenly Susan.” She earned Emmy nominations for the TV adaptation of “Breaking Away,” as well as for her appearances on “Law & Order” and “Law & Order: SVU.” Barrie was born on May 23, 1931, in Chicago, and grew up in Texas. She graduated from the University of Texas in 1952 with a major in drama. articles.content: Hayden Panettiere ‘s death has been ruled as accidental and the investigation has concluded, the Greenville, South Carolina police department announced Wednesday. “Based on the (coroner’s office’s) determination and the findings of the investigation, Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled accidental. The award recognizes Kamiński’s exceptional contribution to the art of cinematography and his visionary approach to shaping the visual language of modern filmmaking. He will receive the honor at the Toruń Camerimage festival on Nov. 7. The acclaimed Polish filmmaker is among the most influential cinematographers in contemporary cinema. The Hellraiser reboot director will helm the follow-up to 2024’s Smile 2 for Paramount. Nick Antosca will pen the script. articles.title: TV Ratings: Why Fox News Suffered Its Largest Pre-Election Month Drop in the Past Decade
articles.summary: It still leads rivals MS NOW and CNN by wide margins, however.
articles.content: In the “two things can be true” category: Fox News still holds sizable ratings leads in cable news over CNN and MS NOW . It also suffered the largest year-to-year ratings drop in the month before an election in the past 10 years. Nielsen ratings for October show Fox News averaging 1.68 million viewers in primetime and 1.01 million for the full day. Both are comfortably ahead of MS NOW (925,000 primetime, 588,000 full day) and CNN (598,000, 402,000). In the key news demographic of adults 25-54, things are a bit closer, but Fox’s totals of 145,000 in primetime and 98,000 for the total day still lead. CNN had 107,000 in the demo in primetime and 60,000 for the full day to 95,000 and 62,000 for MS NOW. Fox also had the five most watched cable news shows, led by The Five at 2.7 million daily viewers. Fox News is also touting its online strength, citing 3.8 billion YouTube views for 2026 so far (as measured by social media analytics firm Emplifi) to 2.96 billion for MS NOW and 2.36 billion for CNN. As for the second true thing: In the past decade, none of the three biggest cable news outlets have suffered a decline in the month before a national election as big as Fox News did this year. Compared to October 2025, Fox News slipped by 28 percent in primetime viewers and 27 percent for the full day. The networks’ adults 25-54 audience fell by more than 30 percent. MS NOW and CNN both had double digit percentage gains in primetime vs. a year earlier; MS NOW also did so for the full day, while CNN had a more modest 3 percent bump. Pundits and media analysts have suggested that President Trump’s low approval ratings and an election cycle that seems to favor Democrats may have contributed to the drop at Fox News. Nielsen data doesn’t explain why people watch or don’t watch certain programs or networks, obviously. But the change is a stark one. articles.content: Ernie Johnson, the long-serving host of Inside the NBA on TNT and ESPN , is stepping down. Johnson became host of Inside the NBA with its second season in 1990 and has been at the helm ever since, wrangling and playing off of analysts Kenny Smith (since 1998), Charles Barkley (since 2000) and Shaquille O’Neal (since 2011). “I’ve long described it as a ‘get to’ job — I’m still amazed I get to do this for a living,” Johnson said in the video (watch it in full below). “… This will be my last season. Now after 37 seasons, it’s time.” Barkley pre-empted Johnson’s announcement somewhat in September, saying that he planned to retire from Inside the NBA alongside Johnson after the 2026-27 season. “Right now, unless Ernie changes his mind, next year is my last year for 100%,” Barkley said on The Bill Simmons Podcast . In his announcement, Johnson also cited some recent health issues “a contributing factor” in his decision. The 70-year-old Johnson had heart bypass surgery in 2025, and while he said he feels “great” and isn’t under doctor’s orders to scale back, he wants to use more of his time to be with his family, including his five grandchildren. articles.content: Netflix has signed an exclusive overall deal with Joseph Kay, the creator and showrunner of the medical drama Transplant , which landed on NBC stateside. As part of the deal, Kay will develop and write new TV series for Netflix in Canada, starting with an untitled new family drama. He most recently worked with Netflix as a consulting producer on North of North season 2, the Arctic-set comedy also on the CBC and set to return on Nov. 5. Also for Netflix, he co-executive produced the upcoming adaptation of Carley Fortune’s bestselling novel, This Summer Will Be Different. Transplant, which ran for four seasons, was a medical procedural about a Syrian refugee working as a doctor in a Toronto trauma unit. The drama centered on Dr. Bashir “Bash” Hamed (Hamza Haq, Quantico ), a Syrian doctor with battle-tested skills in emergency medicine who fled his country with his younger sister, Amira (Sirena Gulamgaus). Together they struggled to build a new life in Canada while Bash strived to rebuild his career in medicine. Transplant was produced by Sphère Média Plus, in association with CTV and NBCUniversal International Studios. “I am beyond grateful and thrilled to partner with this incredible company. I have huge admiration for Netflix’s entire team, and for their unsurpassed drive to tell great stories and connect with audiences around the world,” Kay said in a statement on Wednesday. His TV writing credits include Ransom, This Life and Republic of Doyle. “Joe is a seasoned and gifted creator and showrunner, who is also adept at supporting other writers. articles.title: ‘The Birds’ Series With Sarah Snook in the Works at HBO

articles.content: HBO has pecked picked up a limited series project based on The Birds for development. Sarah Snook is attached to star in the drama, an adaptation of Daphne du Maurier’s story and the 1963 Alfred Hitchcock film based on the book. Tom Spezialy ( The Leftovers, Ash vs. Evil Dead ) is writing The Birds and executive producing with Snook and David Heyman (the Harry Potter franchise). The Birds is a co-production of Universal Global Television , which began shopping the series to potential buyers in the summer, and HBO. She was also an Emmy nominee this year for Peacock’s All Her Fault , which was produced by Universal Global TV predecessor Universal International Studios. articles.title: Disney Theme Parks Division Eliminates at Least 100 Jobs
articles.summary: The layoffs follow an early retirement offer made in August The post Disney Theme Parks Division Eliminates at Least 100 Jobs appeared first on TheWrap .
articles.content: The Walt Disney Company’s theme parks division laid off between 100 and 200 people on Wednesday, TheWrap has learned. The staff cuts reportedly followed a regular evaluation of the division’s investments and pending projects, with the entertainment conglomerate having more theme parks-set projects in the works than in the past. It’s said all affected employees were slated to be informed by end of day on Wednesday. The layoffs impacted those across all parts of Imagineering, which is the creative and technical arm that brings to life theme parks, attractions, resorts, cruise ships and live entertainment. While the theme parks division brought in $36.2 billion in revenue in 2025 and made up more than 56% of the company’s operating income, Disney offered voluntary early retirement packages in August to executives as part of a cost-reduction effort. “Over the past few years, we’ve made real changes to how we operate, and we’re still in that process,” Chief People Officer Sonia Coleman wrote in a staff memo at the time. “As you heard on our most recent earnings call, we’re focused on meaningfully reducing costs as part of our ongoing transformation, so we can continue to invest in the areas that will drive our future growth: content, technology, and experiences. We’ve been evaluating a range of options, and the next phase includes introducing a Voluntary Early Retirement Offer (VERO) for a defined group of eligible executives.” The offer, which served as an indication that additional staff cuts were looming at the time, followed a year of significant layoffs at the company. As we previously reported , Disney eliminated 1,000 roles in April. Then, months later in July, another round of cuts occurred. In September, a third round of layoffs impacted an additional couple hundred employees, mainly in the tech and HR areas. The Los Angeles Times first reported word of the new job cuts at Disney. Drew Taylor contributed reporting for TheWrap.

articles.content: Nick Antosca will write the upcoming horror sequel with creator Parker Finn producing Veteran horror filmmaker David Bruckner is set to direct Paramount’s upcoming horror sequel “Smile 3,” taking over from series creator Parker Finn, who will remain on the project as a producer with Temple Hill Entertainment. Nick Antonsca will write the screenplay from a framework developed by Finn. Jonathan Fass is executive producer. Bruckner got his start directing in horror anthology films like “V/H/S,” “Southbound,” and the 2007 Sundance film “The Signal.” His most recent films include “The Night House,” which was released by Searchlight in 2021, and a reimagining of Clive Barker’s “Hellraiser,” which was released by Hulu in 2022. articles.summary: The character actress death was "medically assisted" following a terminal cancer diagnosis.
articles.content: Barbara Barrie , a character actress best known for playing boisterous moms in “ Breaking Away ” and “ Private Benjamin ,” has died. She was 95. Barrie’s daughter, Jane Harnick, told the New York Times that her mother had terminal cancer and said her death was “medically assisted.” Barrie was an inveterate scene stealer who was a frequent presence on stage and screen. On Broadway, she appeared in the original cast of Stephen Sondheim’s “Company,” a revolutionary musical that examined relationships and commitment. Barrie earned a Tony Award nomination for her role in the 1970 production. Other Broadway credits included Neil Simon’s hit “California Suite.” For her film work, Barrie won the best actress prize at the 1964 Cannes Film Festival for “One Potato, Two Potato,” an interracial romance, in which her character confronts prejudice while falling in love with a Black man. But it was “Breaking Away,” and her work as the blue-collar mother of a cycling enthusiast, that put Barrie on the map. She was nominated for best supporting sctress for the 1979 coming-of-age classic, then reprised the part in a 1980 TV series based on “Breaking Away,” earning an Emmy nomination. Barrie also was known to audiences for her turn on the 1970s detective sitcom “ Barney Miller ,” portraying the wife of the title character. Other credits included the films “Judy Berlin,” “The Bell Jar,” and Disney’s “Hercules,” as well as appearances on “Law & Order” and “Suddenly Susan.” Barrie was a published author. She wrote children’s books, as well as “Second Act” and “Don’t Die of Embarrassment,” which examined her battle with colorectal cancer. articles.summary: "Sanxingdui: Future Past," a fully AI-generated feature, made just $181K in its opening weekend in Chinese theaters against a budget of $1.5 million.
articles.content: One of the old adages of the film business was that people wouldn’t pay to watch an actor in theaters if they could see them for free on TV. Today, AI -generated content in China is ubiquitous, with a recent report suggesting that among the explosion of microdramas in China, nearly two-thirds of those videos are all generated by AI. But it seems there’s a big difference between what audiences, even Chinese ones, will pay to buy a ticket for compared to what they will consume on their phones for free. This past weekend, a fully, AI-generated feature film titled “Sanxingdui: Future Past” opened in Chinese theaters and grossed just RMB1.21 million, which is about $181,000, according to the film’s producer Bona Film Group. It’s the first AI feature to get the right to play on Chinese screens, and it makes it a big flop, as Bona in a recent blog post said the budget for the movie was 10 million yuan, which is about $1.5 million. The Kinky Pleasures of ‘Night Terrors’ That’s about the budget of a small indie, and perhaps more than you would’ve guessed when so much of the narrative around AI is that it’s going to cut costs and that you can make “Avatar” for next to nothing. But Bona says the film was produced over the course of two years from a team of 70 to 80 people, and some of the creators bristled at the idea that the images were created with a single click. In fact, the blog post says “Future Past” was being tweaked and technically still “shooting” up until a week before the film hit theaters. articles.title: Slamdance Names Screenplay Competition Winners for 2026 — Read the Full List
articles.summary: James Oxyer’s thriller “Termite” won the $10,000 grand prize, while Wes Andre Goodrich’s “Citizens” took first place in the feature category.
articles.content: A stranger hiding inside the walls is just the beginning of the trouble in this year’s Slamdance screenplay competition grand prize winner. IndieWire can exclusively announce that James Oxyer’s “Termite” has earned the contest’s top accolade, with a story about a lonely teenager whose unexpected houseguest sets the stage for an increasingly fraught drama. AGBO hosted the 2026 winners at an awards ceremony in downtown Los Angeles Tuesday night. That’s the independent studio founded by “Avengers: Endgame” directors Anthony and Joe Russo. AGBO chief creative officer Angela Russo-Otstot welcomed the honorees and presented the night’s biggest award, worth $10,000. Related Stories ACE Eddie Awards Will Honor John Carpenter as Filmmaker of the Year Sundance Reveals First 2027 Legacy Films for Boulder Debut: ‘Y Tu Mamá También,’ ‘Memento,’ and More Now in its 29th year, Slamdance ’s annual screenplay competition received nearly 5,000 submissions from around the world in 2026. This year’s contest recognized emerging writers across feature scripts, a dedicated horror/thriller race, TV pilots, short films, and a special screenplay mentorship category, giving out more than $18,000 in prizes. To date, the awards program reports it has distributed more than $450,000 to emerging filmmakers. “Termite,” which also won first place in the horror/thriller competition, follows a teenager who discovers a homeless man has taken refuge in the walls of his family home. articles.title: ACE Eddie Awards Will Honor John Carpenter as Filmmaker of the Year
articles.summary: Editors Bonnie Koehler, ACE, and Christopher Nelson, ACE, will receive career achievement honors.
articles.content: The 2027 American Cinema Editors (ACE) Eddie Awards will, at least a little, be one for horror freaks. John Carpenter will receive the ACE Golden Eddie Filmmaker of the Year award. The winners will also be announced in 14 competitive categories recognizing the year’s best film editing achievements in film and television. Bonnie Koehler, ACE, and Christopher Nelson, ACE, will receive ACE Career Achievement awards. Carpenter joins an impressive group of Golden Eddie award recipients including Ang Lee, Jon M. Chu, John Waters, Gina Prince-Bythewood, Spike Lee, Quentin Tarantino, Kathleen Kennedy, Christopher Nolan, Lauren Shuler Donner, Guillermo del Toro, Steven Spielberg, Vince Gilligan, Alexander Payne, J.J. Abrams, Nancy Meyers, Martin Scorsese, Norman Jewison, Robert Zemeckis, George Lucas, and the Sundance Institute, among many others. articles.title: Watermelon Pictures to Offer Discounted Tickets, Free Streaming for Gaza Doc ‘American Doctor’ Before Election Day
articles.summary: Exclusive: The Sundance documentary follows three physicians as they advocate for Palestinian colleagues and patients.
articles.content: Advocacy-focused Watermelon Pictures is temporarily waiving its theatrical film rental fees and box office revenue share for the documentary “ American Doctor ,” giving venues the option to offer discounted or free tickets. The campaign will span roughly 50 cities and run through the week of the United States’ midterm elections, from October 30 to November 5. Watermelon hopes to expand the film’s reach to spotlight the humanitarian crisis in Gaza, which “American Doctor” documents through the perspectives of three physicians traveling to the region to provide medical aid. In addition to discounted theatrical admissions, Watermelon is also making “American Doctor” available to stream free for one week on its streaming platform, Watermelon+ , giving access to non-subscribers for a limited time. The free Watermelon+ release runs from October 30 to November 6. A video on-demand release will follow on November 10. articles.title: Roberto Rossellini Retrospectives Head to New York and L.A. for the Italian Neorealist Master’s 120th Birthday
articles.summary: Film Forum in New York, the Italian Ministry of Culture, and Cinecittà will present Rossellini 120, a 25-film retrospective dedicated to Roberto Rossellini, opening November 20 at Film Forum.
articles.content: Italian neorealist master Roberto Rossellini , though he died in 1977, turns 120 this year. In celebration, major retrospective series are coming up. Film Forum in New York, the Italian Ministry of Culture, and Cinecittà will present “Rossellini 120,” a 25- film retrospective dedicated to Roberto Rossellini, opening at Film Forum on November 20. The retrospective will also open in Los Angeles on November 4 at the Academy Museum as “Roberto Rossellini Prefers Real Life,” courtesy of the Italian Ministry of Culture and Cinecittà. Through December 10, New York’s Film Forum will host the 25-film “Rossellini 120.” The filmmaker’s daughter, Oscar-nominated actress Isabella Rossellini, will appear in person on November 20 with “Voyage to Italy” (which starred her mother, Ingrid Bergman, opposite George Sanders) and again on November 26 (i.e., Thanksgiving) with “Flowers of St. Francis” and “Europa ’51.” IndieWire shares exclusive details as well as a trailer for the retrospective above. articles.title: ‘The Gilded Age’ Cast on Returning for Season 4 After a Ratings Surge: ‘It’s Go Big or Go Home’
articles.summary: Carrie Coon, Cynthia Nixon, Morgan Spector, Julian Fellowes and more on the marital problems, blowout parties, and social scandals in store for the HBO hit.
articles.content: The women of “ The Gilded Age ” are assembled in the lavishly appointed drawing room of the Fifth Avenue Hotel for a postmortem. “I’m still buzzing from the other night,” Marceline Hugot, who plays Mrs. Foster, the director of the Heritage Society, says as she rises to address the group. “Despite some hiccups, President Cleveland was charmed.” With that, the camera pulls back, and Gladys Russell (Taissa Farmiga) enters, eliciting upturned eyebrows and side glances as she makes excuses for her absent mother, Bertha Russell, whose rise to the top of society has consumed much of the HBO series’ three previous seasons. But as she begins to describe the headache that has waylaid Bertha, Farmiga’s words grow entangled, and she blows her lines. Related Stories Hoorae’s Microdramas Found 580 Million Views. Can TikTok Get Hollywood Working Again? — Watch ‘The Gilded Age’ Review: Season 4 Is Team Bertha’s Time to Shine “Damn it,” Farmiga exclaims, using a word that would cause any one of these ladies who lunch to stagger back toward their settee in shock. Farmiga grabs her script. Races through the dialogue out loud. Then exits the room to make her entrance again as a makeup artist appears to administer touch-ups and a wardrobe assistant swoops in to adjust one of the women’s hats. As fans of the show know, every detail on “ The Gilded Age ” has to be just right. Bringing the 19th century to life requires a small army of costumers, builders, technicians, and researchers.
